display.title: The Song of Eicha: Music, Hope and Tisha B'Av
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains why music is a gift from Hashem, shares the ancient tune of Eicha, and explains how Tisha B'Av is kept when it falls on Shabbos.
display.summary_long: A Tisha B'Av segment from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, framed by the chanting of Eicha. Uncle Yossi explains that music is one of Hashem's greatest gifts: it can lift a person up or bring him down, which is why the Levi'im sang in the Beis HaMikdash, and why 'Az Yashir' hints at the song we will sing when Moshiach comes. Though we have not listened to music during the Three Weeks, there is one tune we sing even on Tisha B'Av: the age-old melody of Eicha, a song of exile, hope and prayer, ending with 'Hashiveinu'. He then explains that this year Tisha B'Av falls on Shabbos, so the fast is postponed to Sunday and begins right after Shabbos, when everyone goes to shul for Maariv and Eicha. He prays that Hashem turn Tisha B'Av into a day of rejoicing.
display.lesson: Even in golus the Jewish people sing a song of hope, and we pray that Hashem turn Tisha B'Av into a Yom Tov.

date.note: Date of episode 337; confirmed by 'this coming Shabbos is Tisha B'Av' (9 Av 5748 fell on Shabbos).
